title: Uniform stable pages and natural graded comparisons for etale complexes
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category, $D:I\to\mathrm{Sch}$ a diagram [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $c$ a cone. Let $F_i$ be complexes of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], uniformly zero below $a$, with inverse-image maps satisfying identity and composition. Let $G$ identify with their pullbacks to $c$ compatibly, and $L$ be a colimit cocone. For integers $p,q$ and the canonical derived cohomology pullback $P$, there are spectral sequences for the stages and $L$, compatible maps to the limit sequence, ordinary cohomology first-page identifications and their naturality equations, and vanishing in negative resolution degree. There are bounded-below presentations $T_i,T$ and one integer $N\ge1$ identifying the $(p-q,q)$ terms with the $q$-th graded pieces of their degree-$p$ filtrations [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. Transition and comparison maps restrict to all filtration steps, commute with their successive-step inclusions, and under these stable-page identifications induce the corresponding cokernel maps. This statement makes no assertion identifying the filtration with the image-filtration predicate.

proof.text:
Use the functorial Cartan--Eilenberg presentations of
`exists_etaleHypercohomology_pullback_functorial`. Give each F_i its bounded-below
structure with bound a. Inverse image is exact, and colimits of complexes are degreewise,
so L.pt has the same lower bound. The identity and composition equations for φ make
its page maps a functor; the equations for G and the cocone make the limit maps compatible.
Swap the two bidegree coordinates to put the resolution degree first. The first-page
identifications and their two naturality equations are the corresponding equations of
the pullback presentations. Their negative resolution degrees vanish. In bidegree
(p-q,q), incoming and outgoing differentials vanish once the page exceeds both the
resolution degree and the distance q-a to the bottom row. This bound depends only on
p,q,a, and therefore works simultaneously for all stages and the limit. Functorial
convergence identifies this page with the q-th graded piece of each presentation's
canonical image filtration. The filtered total maps restrict to all filtration steps;
their inclusion equations identify the abutment maps with P followed by the coefficient
map. Monicity gives the square for successive steps. Naturality of the stable-page
identification gives precisely cokernel.map on the associated graded pieces.
